title: kernel-lane-pad-savings-bucketing-scheduler
author: Jordan Lin
release_notes: Introduce kernel-lane-aware bucketing scheduler to reduce padding overhead.
Add pad-savings estimator to prefer co-located requests that unlock kernel lane utilization.
No API changes; rollout flag gated behind runtime.feature.kernel_lane_bucketing.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a kernel-lane-aware bucketing scheduler and a pad-savings estimator to the continuous batching pipeline. The goal is to reduce wasted padding across mixed sequence length workloads by preferring batch compositions that simultaneously align to kernel lane widths (vector lane / warp-like constraints) and maximize reuse of KV/prefix cache entries.

Motivation: On modern GPU runtimes we observed microsecond-level inefficiencies that multiply into meaningful token-costs for high QPS services. Two root causes: (1) padding to the longest sequence in a slot leads to wasted compute and memory traffic, and (2) kernels provide best throughput when sequence dimensions align to internal lane widths (e.g., multiples of 8/16 tokens for certain fused-attention kernels).

Design:
- Add a lightweight pad-savings estimator that computes a per-request expected padding penalty for candidate slot compositions. The estimator uses the request seqlen, recent seqlen distribution histograms, and model kernel lane parameters queried from kernel caps metadata.
- Implement a kernel-lane-aware bucketing step before the existing bucket scheduler. Buckets are annotated with preferred lane alignment (e.g., lane_mod = 8). When composing batches, the scheduler prefers combinations that achieve zero or minimal lane_mod remainder while also minimizing total padding.
- Integrate kernel-lane bucketing with the continuous batching window: the scheduler runs as a scoring pass over current cohort, scoring candidates by combined pad-savings + lane-alignment bonus + cache-reuse penalty. A tunable weighting parameter controls tradeoffs.
- KV cache / prefix interaction: to avoid extra cache churn we add a small affinity bonus when requests share identical or strongly overlapping prefix keys (same conversation id or cached embedding id). The scheduler will prefer coalescing these when it does not dramatically increase padding.

Implementation notes:
- New files: runtime/scheduler/kernel_lane_bucketer.rs, runtime/scheduler/pad_savings_estimator.rs, runtime/scheduler/integration.rs (glue), tests/bench/kernel_lane_bucketer_integ.test, docs/perf/notes/kernel-lane-bucketing.md
- The estimator is pure-C, no locks; it reads model kernel metadata from the existing runtime model manifest cache (no schema change).
- Added feature flag runtime.feature.kernel_lane_bucketing (off by default for gradual rollout).
- Configs: default lane weight = 0.75, cache affinity bonus = 0.5, pad weight = 1.0.

Benchmarks:
- Mixed seqlen synthetic workload (poisson arrival, seqlen mix 8/32/128): median latency at steady QPS improved by 6.8%, p99 down 9.2% for single-GPU runs.
- Token compute cost (measured as effective GPU token-seconds) reduced by 12–18% depending on cluster packing.
- Small uniform short-seq workloads unchanged (regression <= 1%).
- Kernel alignment wins were most pronounced on fused-attention kernels that favor 16-token multiples.

CI and validation:
- Unit tests for estimator math and bucketing decisions
- Integration bench harness added and run on perf-canary
- End-to-end e2e test with KV cache overlap scenarios
- CI checks: build, unit, integration, perf-smoke (all passing after two reruns)

Commits summary:
- "introduce pad-savings estimator and kernel lane bucketer" (core logic)
- "add integration glue to continuous batch composer" (integrate with existing window)
- "tests: unit + integration + perf-smoke harness"
- "docs: perf notes and rollout guide"

Changed areas (high level):
- runtime/scheduler/* (new files and small modifications to composer)
- runtime/model/manifest.rs (read-only metadata read path added)
- runtime/config/defaults.toml (feature flag + weights)
- docs/perf/*
- tests/bench/*
- CI workflow: .github/workflows/perf-canary.yml (hooked up to new bench)

Review conversation:
- Ava Chen: "Can you quantify cost of estimator itself? we don't want scheduler CPU to become bottleneck." Author response (Jordan Lin): "Estimator is O(n_candidates) with very cheap ops; in perf runs the added CPU was <2% of scheduler budget. Added microbench numbers to docs."
- Diego Morales: "How does this interact with existing slot-duration packing heuristics?" Author: "We run lane-aware bucketing as a pre-pass scoring step; slot-duration and burst packing remain unchanged. Added comments and a small refactor to keep separation."
- Priya Nambiar: "Feature flagging and rollout criteria? Need safe defaults for dedicated clusters." Author: "Flag off by default. Added a staged rollout doc with metrics to watch: pad_ratio, token_seconds_per_second, p99 latency. Added a kill-switch via runtime admin endpoint."
- Diego Morales (post-approve): "Approve after CI green and add docs about the model manifest field required." Author: "Acknowledged; manifest metadata addition is backward compatible and documented."

CI checks: - build: pass - unit: pass - integration: pass - perf-smoke: pass (two reruns after flakiness on perf harness)

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-03-07.

Rollout notes:
- Start with 5% of requests on hosted clusters with low variance seqlen and monitor pad_ratio and token_seconds.
- Enable cache-affinity only after confirming low churn.
- If regressions appear, reduce lane weight or disable feature flag.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: estimator misweights short bursts, causing slight latency regressions for purely short-seq traffic. Mitigation: default weights tuned conservatively; feature flag.
- Risk: model manifest missing kernel lane metadata on older models. Mitigation: fallback to conservative lane_mod=8 default and emit a one-time warning metric.

Follow-ups (future PRs):
- Auto-tune lane weight using rolling pad_ratio signal
- Add GPU-side hints to kernels to accept soft-padding for fractional lanes
- Extend estimator to consider memory bandwidth impact for long-context models
